accuracy.evidence: Vocabulary matches the PSHE Association Programme of Study KS1 (Health and wellbeing: keeping safe; Relationships: making choices, right and wrong, rules) and the DfE statutory Relationships Education guidance for primary (being honest, how to ask for help from a trusted adult, recognising when a situation feels unsafe). Trusted adults named are parent, grandparent, teacher and police officer, consistent with NSPCC PANTS and 'trusted adult' guidance; strangers are never framed as trusted however friendly.

misconceptions.evidence: Targets the named slips: consequence means punishment only (fork walks show a happy friend for giving the ball back; prediction 'Do good choices have consequences too?'; m1, m5), rules only stop fun (m2 hold hands by the road), honesty always gets you in trouble (prediction 'You tell the truth about a mistake', m6, honest-words step), and friendly means trusted (strangers bounced from the safe circle with feedback, m3 puppy lure, p4).

lab_distinct.evidence: New mechanics for this topic: dragging a child figure down both roads of a fork to watch each consequence play out, a consequence-card sorter, choosing honest words in three mistake scenes, dragging people into a safe circle where strangers bounce back, and a picture-word match for fair, honest, rule, safe, responsible. Passed the 30% shingle gate; flagcause, flagassert and flagaware cover feelings and fairness, not choice-consequence or trusted adults.

lab_teaches.evidence: The child experiences each word before being told it: they walk the fork and see the consequence, then the step names it; they choose words after breaking something and see the honest choice lead to help; they discover by trying that a smiling stranger will not go in the safe circle. Step summaries say the word only after the task is done, with picture support for pre-readers.

predictions.evidence: Two locked predictions with tempting wrong answers for this age: 'Do good choices have consequences too?' (tempting: no, consequences are punishments; the next fork walk shows a happy friend) and 'You tell the truth about a mistake. What happens?' (tempting: you get in big trouble; the honest-words step shows a grown-up helping fix it).

challenge_feedback.evidence: Five rotating challenge questions with eleven distinct feedback messages, e.g. 'Friendly is not the same as trusted', 'Good choices have consequences too', 'Rules keep us safe, not stop fun', and 'Telling the truth helps people trust you', each tied to the specific wrong option chosen.

readability.evidence: learn/readability.py: kid text 0.9 (family limit 5.0), adult text 7.6 (limit 10.0). Canvas labels are one to three words with an emoji picture each; the young class enlarges text and tap targets; instructions are one short line such as 'Drag the grown-ups you trust into the circle'.

no_filler.evidence: Passed the filler regex and the 12% duplicate gate. Each kid paragraph adds one word group (choice and consequence, good consequences, honest, rule/fair/responsible, trusted adult); the adult text gives the age range and vocabulary list, the choice-consequence link with a question to ask, four named mistakes including the friendly-stranger slip, and the lab outline.

mobile.evidence: Screenshots of all six steps at 360 px light (android profile) and iPhone 13 dark (shot.cjs): fork roads, consequence cards and bins, honest-word options, the safe circle with people around it and the five picture-word pairs fit with no clipping. Young-class buttons are large tap targets and every canvas action is repeated as a button below the canvas.

accessibility.evidence: walk.cjs passed on desktop and iPhone 13: all tasks complete with Show me, the challenge shows, axe WCAG 2.1 AA clean in light and dark, no console or page errors. Every drag has a button route (road buttons, Good/Bad buttons, word buttons, one button per person, tap word then picture). The canvas aria-label restates each task and each result.

sources: Department for Education (2019, updated 2021), Relationships Education, Relationships and Sex Education and Health Education: statutory guidance (primary: being safe, honesty, asking a trusted adult for help)
PSHE Association, Programme of Study for PSHE Education Key Stages 1-5 (KS1 H/R learning opportunities on rules, choices and keeping safe)
NSPCC, Talk PANTS and guidance on trusted adults for young children
RoSPA, road safety advice for young children (holding hands near roads, cycle helmets)
